### [1/3] MEASURED FACTS — do not re-derive

PROBLEM: tickets branch = 1.04 GiB; 92% is the reconciler .bridge_state cache. Object attribution on ONE 51-day denominator: bindings.json 828.3 MB (16.2 MB/day), prev_snapshot.json 228.1 MB (4.5), event *.json 55.0 MB (1.08), commits/trees 15.5 MB (0.30), other 25.8 MB (0.51, still unattributed).

ROOT CAUSE (measured): per-pass churn in bindings.json across consecutive committed revisions = baseline VALUE changed 0 entries; `baseline_advanced_at` (written once at binding_store.py:375, read NOWHERE in src/) changed 1144; `last_get_pass` changed 20. ~100% of growth is bookkeeping no consumer reads, scattered across a sort-ordered 18 MB file, defeating delta compression.

FIX EFFECT (40 consecutive real revisions rebuilt in a clean repo, repacked --window=250 --depth=50, marginal = (pack_N - pack_1)/(N-1)):
  as-committed  40/40 distinct versions  12.79 KB/version  499 KB
  A1 only       40/40                     1.74 KB           68 KB  (7.4x)
  A1 + A2       20/40                     2.05 KB           39 KB  (12.8x)
CAVEAT: the measurement models A1 as DELETING the field. Since baseline value changes are 0, the write-when-changed guard is byte-neutral today - the measured win is the deletion.

CLONE COST vs GitHub: full 1.04 GiB / 59s wall / 319s CPU; --filter=blob:none 68.7 MiB / 14.3s; --filter=blob:limit=1m 72.1 MiB / 13.2s. Whole-store verify-identity in a blob:none clone fetched 0 BYTES and ran FASTER than full (3.75s vs 3.98s): its scan is a pure tree-level diff and event/keyring bodies are read from the WORKING TREE (verify_authorship.py:371, authorship.py:119-128).

prev_snapshot key-set (newest 400 revisions): 218/399 consecutive pairs have an IDENTICAL key set (become byte-identical, no commit); mean symmetric difference when it changes = 1.78 keys; key-set payload at HEAD = 19,960 bytes vs 27.1 MB full.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
### [2/3] CORRECTED FALSE PREMISES — three errors caught by adversarial review, all previously believed true

E1. "A history rewrite creates UNRELATED histories, so sync.py:96's no-merge-base branch fires." FALSE. `.bridge_state` first appears 2026-06-11, so the first 1,029 commits are BYTE-IDENTICAL after a strip and `merge-base HEAD origin/tickets` SUCCEEDS (measured). Control reaches the ordinary DIVERGED path (sync.py:100-112) and unions normally. The hazard is real; the mechanism was mis-identified. Quiescence alone does NOT close it.

E2. "A guard in sync.py protects all writers." FALSE. push.py:203 and :229 run an INDEPENDENT `git merge <remote>/<branch>` on non-fast-forward rejection and then re-push (<=3 attempts), never consulting sync.py. That is exactly the path a stale review-bot write takes: voter.py:735 -> create_ticket -> push_after_commit -> push_tickets_branch -> rejected -> push.py:203 merge -> retry SUCCEEDS. A sync-only guard is bypassed and ~1 GiB returns silently.

E3. "Text-normalizing the baseline needs no migration because _extract_jira_field reads both shapes." FALSE-ish: `_extract_jira_field`/`_diff_fields` have ZERO production callers. The live path is outbound_field_diff.py:194 -> inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local -> inbound_fields.py. Description/status/priority ARE safe there (canonicalized at READ time, idempotent on already-normalized values). ASSIGNEE IS NOT: _assignee_candidates (outbound_field_diff.py:56-67) unions the scalar with every non-None identity form; collapsing three forms to one string loses inbound-directionality suppression and local-wins silently CLOBBERS a concurrent remote assignee edit. Exclude assignee.

ALSO CORRECTED: (a) rebar NEVER clones - `grep 'git clone' src/` yields only a docstring - so it cannot filter a clone it does not perform; only the actions/checkout `filter:` input reduces a real transfer, and the tickets objects arrive in that 237s checkout step, NOT the 2s manual worktree mount. (b) `_ref_lock.py:347` is NOT a tickets fetch (it fetches refs/reconciler/{lock,gate}, read back via `cat-file blob`); filtering it would add promisor round-trips to the distributed lock. (c) `git blame` IS on a rebar path - metrics/blame.py:69 <- derive_caused_by <- transition_close.py:513, on every bug close without --caused-by - and PARTIAL blame failure is not benign: derive_caused_by tallies across paths and a subset can elect a culprit that would not have won, i.e. a WRONG caused_by link.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
### [3/3] PRIOR ART + THE RECLAIM DECISION

PRIOR ART (cited): crates.io index (31 squashes since 2018; RFC 2789 says "shallow clones and history squashing offer only temporary relief"; snapshot branches MOVED to a separate repo in 2022 because "the server still has to consider their contents whenever Cargo asks for master" - 1.73 GB live vs 6.94 GB archive), Homebrew 4.0 (JSON over CDN; earlier hard-banned shallow clones at GitHub's request, generating a `critical`-labelled message rewrite in 4 days and a thread locked "too heated"), CocoaPods (shallow clones CAUSED GitHub CPU rate-limiting; still carries a 1.3 GB repo it can never shrink; exit is to freeze and archive Dec 2026), Go module proxy (immutable content-addressed zips; git demoted to a server-side detail). git-filter-repo itself refuses to run outside a fresh clone and directs you to publish a NEW URL and have everyone reclone.
KEY DISQUALIFIER FOUND: every squash case had exactly ONE writer. rebar's tickets branch is multi-writer, converged by --allow-unrelated-histories. No prior art exists for a squash on a merge-replicated multi-writer branch.

RECLAIM: initially dropped on that basis, then RE-ADMITTED by operator decision under an explicit quiescence protocol (paused schedulers + confirmed zero sessions = single-writer for the duration, which IS the precondition prior art required).

MECHANICS PROVEN on the real branch (not theoretical): `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` => 1,172,586,762 -> 98,803,422 bytes (8.4%), all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges preserved, HEAD tree byte-identical except the intended paths, ~30s. No new dependency (git-filter-repo NOT required, and is worse here because it prunes empty commits and would reshape the DAG the ancestry-based trust model walks).

TRUST MODEL VERIFIED SAFE: verify-identity uses git only for ancestry and reads bodies from the working tree; no literal commit SHA is bound anywhere EXCEPT rebar.toml:115 `enforce_since` (the only one; `verify.opcert_enforce_since` is unset). With require_authenticated=false, verify_authorship.py:531-550 returns early and never even reads enforce_since - so no CI deadlock and the re-pin lands normally. Plan-review and completion attestations also survive: they pin CODE SHAs and file-content hashes, never tickets SHAs.

BLOCKERS FOUND AND DESIGNED AROUND: (1) the keystone guard must sit in BOTH union sites - inside sync._union_merge (NOT before sync.py:96, which would block the ff-adopt that a behind clone needs and wedge it forever) AND before push.py:203/:229; (2) it goes in the EXISTING .store-compat.json (compat.py ignores unknown keys - verified - so adding `epoch` cannot crash or fail-close an older binary) with expand/contract: reader ships first, value appears only in the rewrite commit; (3) remote tag pre-heal-a118-20260710T005736Z pins 22,317 commits / 63 MB and MUST be deleted or the reclaim lands at 167 MB not 94 MiB; (4) .bridge_state.bak-retarget/prev_snapshot.json is 33,025,572 bytes sitting in the tree AT HEAD - delete before the strip; (5) the re-add set must be derived DYNAMICALLY (A2-1 adds a 4th file, get_rotation.json).
